build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many shots the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 1430 shots against 1355.9 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. discovery.hypothesis: Pastrnak had 4 or more shots on goal in three straight games and has 61 shots this season, close to double any other Bruin. With Hagens on injured reserve, he may carry even more of the offense. Florida ranks near the bottom of the league in blocked shots.
discovery.question: Can Pastrnak clear 3.5 against a Florida team that allows only 24.6 shots per game, the third-fewest in the league? And is the 3.5 line still available, or has it moved toward the 2.5 that one book listed?

discovery.hypothesis: Covers included Under 6.5 as one leg of a parlay. Its reasoning: Boston allows the fewest 5-on-5 goals per 60 minutes, Florida ranks first in 5-on-5 expected goals against, and Florida's offense is weakened by injuries. Covers also shows Boston going over in only 9 of its last 25 games.
discovery.question: Is the current total 5.5 rather than 6.5? Covers' own betslip shows U5.5 at -105, and Covers' trend lists show the over hitting in Florida's recent games. Either could remove any cushion for the under.
